data.narrative:
Nuro, a Series G autonomous delivery drone company co-founded by Dave Ferguson and Jiajun Zhu, is valued at $6.0B post-money and has raised $2.54B to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 4 comparable companies in the Drones & Autonomous sector, spanning stages from Series D to public listings, with valuations ranging from $3.3B to $8.6B.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, applying a 1.25x multiplier typical for Series G advancement, yields $7.5B. Peer-median triangulation across Wayve ($8.6B), Zipline ($7.6B), Joby Aviation ($6.9B), and Archer Aviation ($3.3B) produces a median of $7.2B. The peer set median of $7.2B closely aligns with stage-progression output, providing methodological consistency.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $6.1B to $8.6B, with a median of $7.4B. The current $6.0B valuation sits at the lower bound of this range. Key uncertainties include execution risk on autonomous delivery commercialization timelines, regulatory approval pathways, and competitive positioning relative to better-capitalized players like Waymo. The wide peer range ($3.3B–$8.6B) reflects sector-wide variance in path-to-profitability assumptions and public market reception of autonomous platforms.
